subject: DPA, SIG/CAIQ & keystore - retention exception request
raw_messages:
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@atlaspay.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@atlaspay.com
Date: 2026-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA & keystore questions for MAP

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for sending over the MAP. Legal reviewed the DPA redline and had a couple of questions before we sign:

- AtlasPay must keep data in EU regions only; can you confirm options for EU-only residency in Redwood Private or hosted? 
- We need BYOK with HSM/KMS: can Redwood support customer-managed keys (BYOK) and provide an HSM-backed keystore?
- Retention exception: we may need a 45-month retention window for historical transaction logs; DPA currently caps at 24 months. Can we get an exception or a tiered retention plan?

Can you loop in engineering and security for technical confirmation? Also would like SOC 2 Type II evidence and a completed SIG/CAIQ matrix.

Regards,
Raj Patel
Head of Legal — AtlasPay
raj.patel@atlaspay.com

Attachments: none

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@atlaspay.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-18T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA & keystore questions for MAP

Thanks Raj — looping in Steph (contracts) and Marcus (infra). Quick summary and next steps below:

- Data residency: Hosted API can be pinned to our eu-west-1 region (data-in-transit and rest), and Redwood Private can be deployed into your EU VPC. Confirm whether you need managed-hosted with EU tenancy or Private (our recommendation for strict residency).

- BYOK / HSM: We do support BYOK on Private deployments and have HSM-backed KMS integrations (HSM via vendor partners). Marcus has attached a short note on options and expected timelines.

- Retention: We can propose a tiered retention addendum — default 24 months with a regulated-data tier up to 48 months for transactional archives. Procurement/legal approval required for retention exceptions.

Attachments:
- DPA_Redline_v3.docx (our current redline)
- kms-integration-notes.pdf (Marcus)

Next steps:
1) Marcus to confirm feasibility and timelines for BYOK (see attachment).
2) Steph to send DPA with proposed retention addendum for legal review / DocuSign.
3) I'll attach SOC2 report and SIG/CAIQ matrix once we have the go-ahead.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

A few clarifications:
- For BYOK — we prefer a vendor HSM with FIPS 140-2 Level 3 and customer key material never exported from our control. Is that supported on Private? 
- On residency: the risk/compliance team insists on an assertion that backups and logs will also remain in EU; are there any cross-region backups for hosted? 
- For the retention addendum: can you put the 48-month tier on a per-dataset basis (payment logs only) and leave user behavioral data at 24 months?

If you can provide SOC2 report and SIG/CAIQ matrix this week, that would help speed legal sign-off.

Thanks,
Raj

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@atlaspay.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-20T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA & keystore questions for MAP — technical notes

Hi Raj,

Thanks — answering from an infra perspective.

- HSM/BYOK: On Redwood Private we can support HSM-backed BYOK where customer keys are injected via an HSM-backed KMS (we integrate with AWS CloudHSM and Azure Dedicated HSM). Keys are customer-held and we do not export key material. FIPS 140-2 Level 3 support is available depending on the cloud provider.

- Backups & logs: For hosted EU tenancy we replicate logs to eu-west-1 only; we do not cross-replicate to other regions by default. For Private, all backups can remain in-customer VPC/region.

- Retention tiering: We can implement dataset-level retention gating. Implementation plan:
  * Week 0–1: confirm dataset list and retention policy mapping
  * Week 2–4: config changes + QA in staging
  * Week 5: deploy to Private / set retention flags for hosted tenancy

Attachments: kms-integration-notes.pdf (detailed), SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf (redacted)

If you want a formal runbook for key rotation and incident response, we can produce one in the next sprint.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
